title: 40th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened with the Speaker's announcements, and an urgent motion by an MDP member asking the government to disclose its political appointees was voted down 8 to 59. The Finance Minister presented the 2024 supplementary budget of about MVR 5.1 billion, and the house voted 69-0 to debate it from 1:30 pm, send it to the budget committee and give members five minutes each. The house then voted on seven nominees for the Tax Appeal Tribunal, approving four and rejecting three, before the supplementary budget debate began. Government-side members backed the budget, while MDP members questioned debt and how the money is spent; the text of this part ends mid-debate. Members continued debating the Finance Minister's roughly MVR 5.1 billion supplementary budget for 2024. PNC and allied members mostly backed it, saying it covers inherited debts, state-company shortfalls and health cover, while MDP members questioned where the original 2024 budget had gone and raised stalled island projects. Several members also raised unfinished projects in their own constituencies. The chair ended the debate and sent the budget to the Budget Review Committee; the attached vote records also show three Tax Appeal Tribunal nominees approved and one not. The text layer is partly garbled, so speaker gists are approximate. This part of the minutes is made up only of electronic roll-call vote records, with no debate text. It opens with the tail of a roll call whose heading sits in an earlier part, then records three open votes on nominees for the Tax Appeal Tribunal. Two nominees were rejected with 52 and 51 'No' votes, and the third was approved 68-0. Each vote had 78 members present and 77 eligible to vote.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Asked the government to disclose how many political appointees it has made and their roles, and to explain salary cuts.
Said the government should explain how supplementary budget money is spent.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Moved that debate start at 1:30 pm, with five minutes per member, then budget committee review.
Said MDP governments spent supplementary money before parliament approved it, which he said breached the finance law.
Said the current government seeks approval before spending and asked members to back the budget.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Raised a point of order on how the budget debate should proceed.
Criticised the cost of the Tax Appeal Tribunal and the few cases it handles, and supported the nominees.
Said supplementary budgets are not unusual and criticised earlier governments for spending first and seeking approval afterwards.
Said large debt repayments fall due in coming years and backed the president's cost-cutting.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Argued the government should show where the money is spent and said loans have risen to near one billion dollars.
Said salaries cut for politicians and judges, and project progress should be visible to the public.

speakers.name: Moosa Zameer
positions: As Finance Minister, presented the supplementary budget citing medical costs, PSIP project costs and student loans.
Said he would wait while members debated the procedure.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Seconded the procedural motion.
Supported the supplementary budget as a legal requirement and disputed claims that the 2024 budget was used up.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Referred to his earlier work on the budget committee when responding to the minister's budget.
Supported the procedural motion put forward by the majority leader.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the procedural motion on the budget debate.
Said earlier MDP governments also passed supplementary budgets and cited figures for 2019 to 2023.
Said spending then came before parliament approval and money was printed.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Presented the Judiciary Committee report on Tax Appeal Tribunal nominees, listing seven nominees scoring 75% or more.

speakers.name: Yoosuf Nasheed
positions: Raised a point of order saying the claim about loans was false; the chair did not accept it as a point of order.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the budget and said payment delays to contractors and staff made a supplementary budget necessary.
Called for those responsible for earlier irregularities to be held to account.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the budget as meeting legal requirements, and welcomed funding for health and island projects.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Supported the budget, welcoming funds for Addu Equatorial Hospital, and blamed earlier debts for the need.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Voiced concern about the increase in the budget and in government debt, and about project spending.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Supported the budget and said it follows legal procedure, citing unpaid bills from the previous government.

speakers.name: Mohamed Afoo Hamid
positions: Supported the budget and asked for committee review to finish quickly so it can pass.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Supported the budget and linked the need for it to debts left by the previous government.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the budget and said it follows earlier debts and unrecorded bills in the finance ministry.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Supported the budget and compared spending under the previous government with its pledge to cut costs; text ends mid-speech.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Backed the supplementary budget to fund student loans, Aasandha health cover, subsidies and civil service salaries.
Said it stays within the legal limits, unlike practices he attributed to the previous government.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the budget and described state companies such as Fenaka as left heavily indebted by the previous government.
Said projects in his constituency have stalled for lack of funds.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Fully supported the budget; said the previous government spent before parliament approved and left companies like Fenaka and MTCC in debt.
Said fishermen are owed money.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the budget but said contractors and projects in his constituency have received no advance payments.
Called for investigation and prosecution of those accused of harming state finances, and for changes to the Aasandha health insurance scheme.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Said PNC members are not rubber stamps and support the president within the law.
Argued the budget responds to inherited debt and urged members to back the government.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said he did not object to the budget's size but wanted an account of how the existing 2024 budget was spent before more is approved.
Said projects in his constituency have not progressed.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Supported the bill but raised concerns about stalled projects in Thimarafushi and Veymandoo.
Asked for the Veymandoo causeway, road work and 100 housing units to be completed and connected to services.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Supported the supplementary budget, saying previous governments left large state-company debts and unpaid bills.
Said Vilimale' has received little development from successive governments.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Opposed the budget and asked where most of the 2024 budget had gone before more funding is sought.
Listed stalled Kendhoo projects such as the health centre, roads and harbour, and said he would work to stop it passing.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said the supplementary budget is needed because spending requires parliament's approval first.
Said health care funding must continue and criticised undocumented spending by state companies.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the budget and said previous governments also added supplementary budgets.
Said projects in Dhidhdhoo, including a hospital upgrade, stalled and blamed the previous government.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Opposed the budget, saying it adds debt for citizens.
Listed projects not started in Keyodhoo: a school building, council office and health centre.

decisions: Meekail Ahmed Nasym's urgent matter on political appointees was not accepted for debate (8 yes, 59 no).
Debate on the supplementary budget to start at 1:30 pm, five minutes per member, then budget committee (69-0).
Abdul Ghani Mohamed (Hostside) approved as Tax Appeal Tribunal member (68-0).
Ibrahim Shareef (Ilaa) approved as Tax Appeal Tribunal member (68-0).
Hassan Zuhair Mohamed (Maavaru) approved as Tax Appeal Tribunal member (68-0).
Abdul Qayyoom Shifza (Nilandhoo) approved as Tax Appeal Tribunal member (68-0).
Three other Tax Appeal Tribunal nominees were not approved, including Mohamed Ameen Zahir (7-53).
The debate on the 2024 supplementary budget (about MVR 5.1 billion) ended and it was sent to the Budget Review Committee.
Ibrahim Falah's motion on the 2024 supplementary budget passed 69-0.
Meekail Ahmed Nasym's motion to debate an urgent matter was rejected 8-59.
Tax Appeal Tribunal nominees Abdul Ghanee Mohamed, Ibrahim Shareef and Hassan Zuhair Mohamed each received 68 yes votes and none against.
Tax Appeal Tribunal nominee Mohamed Ameen Zahir received 7 yes and 53 no.
The sitting was adjourned until 28 October 2024 at 9:00 am.
Tax Appeal Tribunal nominee Abdulla Abdul Hakeem was not approved (7 yes, 52 no)
Tax Appeal Tribunal nominee Ali Riza Ismail was not approved (8 yes, 51 no)
Tax Appeal Tribunal nominee Shifza Abdul Gayyoom was approved (68 yes, 0 no)
